result.title: Where to Approximate: Understanding and Accelerating Looped Multi-View Reconstruction
result.summary: Looped multi-view reconstruction refines scene features by repeatedly applying a shared transformer block. Making these updates cheaper requires knowing how an approximation at one step affects the rest of the refinement. We study this with paired interventions in Déjà View and stacked reconstruction transformers, separating the error an approximation injects, how that error propagates, and how it affects the output. In Déjà View, approximation errors are attenuated more strongly than matched random perturbations under a scale-adjusted state-error measure, and a local Jacobian decomposition separates the contribution of channel gating from the response to spatial error structure. Spatial approximations made early benefit from subsequent refinement, whereas cross-step reuse depends on which quantity is cached and how reuse steps are spaced. At equal final norm, approximation errors change the predicted rotations 1.55 times as much as random errors. These findings guide our proposed method, which reduces spatial resolution and pools keys and values early in refinement, then interleaves attention-output reuse with full attention, and is adapted through lightweight self-distillation. Across five reconstruction benchmarks, the balanced configuration runs $1.63\times$ faster than the official 16-step Déjà View model with a 1.86-point reduction in average pose AUC@$3^\circ$. At matched latency, it exceeds the interpolated curve of a trained baseline using full refinement blocks by 4.73 points in AUC@$3^\circ$ and improves the corresponding geometry metrics.

AI.brief_summary: 论文以成对干预分析循环式多视图重建中近似误差的注入、传播与输出影响，并据此提出早期降分辨率、KV 池化、注意力输出复用与轻量自蒸馏的加速方案。
AI.relevance_reason: 其关于循环共享块中「何处可近似、缓存哪个量、误差如何随状态传播」的分析，可能为 LVR 循环推理状态的计算分配与状态复用提供核查线索，但未涉及语言或多模态推理与答案使用。
